title: burst-latency-token-cost-simulation-sheet
summary: Simulation-driven comparison of $/token and perf/W for bursty inference patterns across A10, L4, A100, H100. Focus: cold-cache penalties, short-lived bursts (1-10s), and impact on unit economics versus sustained throughput pricing assumptions.
methodology: We run a stochastic discrete-event sim (toy model exported to CSV here) to model request arrivals with Poisson bursts and a background steady traffic. Key variables: seq_length_distribution (short/med/long), model_kv_cache_hit_rate (0-90%), batch_size_policy (auto/fixed), and GPU power draw profiles (idle/active). Per-GPU throughput numbers are derived from microbenchmarks (internal infra tests) for a 13B-ish baseline transformer; prices are synthetic cloud rates to keep internal benchmarks consistent across regions. Sim calculates tokens/sec, tokens/hour, $/token, p95 token latency, and tokens-per-joule.
scenarios:
Scenario A: Short burst spikes (peak 20x baseline) for 3-8s, warm cache 70%.
Scenario B: Cold-start bursts (prefix cache miss) - first 2s of each burst treated as cold (cache miss penalty applied).
Scenario C: Sustained steady state (24/7) for baseline comparison.
Sequence mix: 65% short (<256), 25% medium (256-1024), 10% long (>1024). Batch policy: prefer small batches for latency-sensitive lanes; autoscale to sustain bursts where possible.

# Notes: prices are synthetic and normalized to keep comparisons focused on relative economics rather than absolute cloud region variance.
findings:
1) Per-token marginal cost in the steady-state is similar across instance types given our assumed price points; differences arise from latency and power efficiency.
2) Cold-cache bursts produce the largest effective $/token increase because peak throughput drops and p95 latency spikes; this impacts small-burst use cases (chatty UI) most.
3) A100 shows best tokens-per-joule for sustained workloads; L4 offers the best p95-to-cost ratio for low-latency short bursts under our assumptions.
4) H100 shines for extreme throughput & lowest p95 for long sequences but the higher per-hour cost dilutes marginal $/token advantage for small bursts.
5) Batching helps amortize cold penalties but increases p95; for latency-sensitive lanes small fixed batches + aggressive prefix caching wins.
recommendations:
- For latency-sensitive bursty features (chat, realtime suggest): prefer L4 in single-GPU configs with autoscale cap and aggressive prefix caching. Use small fixed batch sizes (2-4) and warm-up probes to reduce first-token latency.
- For high-throughput steady inference (vectorization, bulk embeddings): use A100 clusters; optimize quantization (INT8/4-bit) where model quality allows.
- For mixed fleets: use smart routing by policy: route latency-critical requests to L4 pool, bulk to A100/H100 pools; fallback to cheaper variants during saturation.
- Invest in a tiny warm-hot cache layer (RAM-based KV cache shard) to knock cold penalty from ~2s to ~150-300ms for typical prompt prefixes — this is highest ROI for $/token on bursty lanes.
- Re-run simulations with real cloud spot pricing curves; current results are sensitive to price assumptions (see appendix).
next_steps:
1) Re-run sim with measured pricedata from us-west-2 (spot + on-demand) and add region-level sensitivity.
2) Hook up real microbench results for our top-3 models (redwood-13b, redwood-7b-quant, open-30b) to replace synthetic throughput.
3) Prototype warm-hot prefix cache (in-memory) and measure cold->warm reduction across 1000 sampled user sessions.
4) Add arrival patterns from product analytics (actual burst shapes) instead of Poisson surrogates.
5) Share with solutions engineering for Dedicated capacity sizing playbook.
comments: Working doc — numbers are intentionally synthetic to focus discussion on shape and sensitivity. Ping @Diego for the sim script and raw CSVs. Looking to lock price assumptions before turning this into an exec-facing brief.
raw_notes:
- Cold penalty modeled as 0.6x throughput and +1500ms p95 for first 2s of a burst.
- Assumed GPU idle baseline power 30% of active.
- Quantization expected to improve tok/s by 1.2-1.6x depending on kernel support.
- Edge case: tiny bursts (<1s) dominated by network/hop latencies; GPU choice less relevant there.
